t: You're at the Prince Consort Gallery, an exhibition space inside the Victoria and Albert Museum. It was built in the Victorian era to show off some of the most valuable things the South Kensington Museum then owned. Later it was reconfigured and used to store part of the museum's textile archive. Today it hosts special events and exhibitions, and now and then it serves as a lunchroom for school groups and staff. It's named for Prince Albert, Queen Victoria's husband, who became Prince Consort in 1857.
